question.problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4},\, & 0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P((X-1)^{2}+{Y}^{2}<1).$
question.worked_solution:
If $f(x,y)$ is a joint probability density function for the random variables $X$ and $Y$ and $A⊂{R}^{2},$ then

$$
P((X,Y)\in A)={∬}_{A}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

Notice that $f(x,y)$ is nonnegative in the region $D=[0,2]\times [0,2],$ and the event $A=\{(X-1)^{2}+{Y}^{2}<1\}$ corresponds to a subset of $D,$ shown as the shaded region below, which is a semicircle of radius $R=1:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14154394/assets/f7f9f016d5f121b2153c1833c959be76f5a11eabb121533dd11839d6da973814.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P((X-1)^{2}+{Y}^{2}<1) & ={∬}_{A}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{∬}_{A}\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\text{Area}(A) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\pi {R}^{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
